RE: Formal Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Reese Mercado
Member ID: W529317483
Reference Number: POC-8AD74FF769-66861
Date of Notice: 2026-08-01
Requested Service/CPT Code: Partial knee replacement / CPT 27446
Treating Surgeon: Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Cigna Appeals Unit:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 27446 (partial knee replacement), as described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-01 (Reference No. POC-8AD74FF769-66861). The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I respectfully disagree and ask that this determination be reversed based on the clinical record summarized below.

Cigna delegates medical-necessity review for knee arthroplasty procedures, including CPT 27446, to EviCore healthcare under guideline CMM-311: Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty. I have reviewed the version of that guideline publicly available at the time of my denial (Version 2.0.2025, effective November 5, 2025), available at:
https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-08/EviCore_CMM-311%20Knee%20Replacement%20Arthroplasty_V2.0.2025_Eff11.05.2025_upd08.12.2025.pdf

I note that I have not received written confirmation from Cigna of the exact policy version or section actually applied to my case. I formally request that Cigna identify, in writing, the specific policy title, number, version, and effective date used to make this determination, and provide a full copy of the criteria applied, so that I may confirm my records are mapped to the correct standard.

Based on the version of CMM-311 I was able to obtain, the guideline states that partial knee replacement "is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met," and I address each below:

1. Imaging/arthroscopic findings of severe unicompartmental osteoarthritis

The guideline requires imaging or arthroscopic findings showing, among other options, "Kellgren-Lawrence Grade IV radiographic findings." My MRI of the knee dated 2026-06-08 documented "full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition" and was read as "Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially." This directly satisfies the imaging criterion described in the policy. The stated denial reason — that "the imaging findings ... do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure" — does not appear consistent with these findings, and I ask the reviewing physician to specifically explain what element of the Kellgren-Lawrence Grade IV, bone-on-bone MRI findings was found insufficient.

2. Physical exam findings

The guideline requires that "Physical exam demonstrates BOTH of the following findings: knee stability; knee arc of motion (full extension to full flexion) >90º." My submitted exam records document "positive provocative testing on the affected side" and range of motion "limited by pain." The record as summarized to me does not contain a specific numeric measurement of my arc of motion or an explicit stability statement. I am asking Dr. Lindqvist to submit a supplemental addendum quantifying my range of motion in degrees and explicitly documenting ligamentous/knee stability testing, so that this criterion can be fully and accurately assessed on appeal. [Supplemental exam addendum to be attached]

3. Symptom criteria

The guideline requires symptoms including "BOTH of the following: function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration; loss of knee function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment." My clinical record documents 24 months of progressive knee pain unrelieved by rest, an inability to climb stairs without assistance, and nighttime awakening 3–4 times per night due to pain — all of which reflect a significant, long-standing loss of function in daily activities. The record as provided to me does not contain a specific quantification of my walking distance tolerance. I am requesting that Dr. Lindqvist supplement the file with a specific statement regarding ambulation distance limitation, to directly mirror the language of this criterion. [Supplemental functional-limitation statement to be attached]

4. Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management

The guideline requires "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months duration." My record reflects the following conservative treatment, well in excess of the three-month requirement:
- NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief;
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-18 providing only 3 weeks of partial relief;
- Supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, 24 visits completed over 8 weeks (2026-05-12 through 2026-07-07), as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

This combination of pharmacologic, injection-based, and supervised physical therapy treatment over many months, without durable improvement, satisfies the guideline's non-surgical management requirement.

5. Additional relevant findings

My record also confirms the absence of any disqualifying condition noted elsewhere in Cigna's clinical criteria: no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI of 29, and non-smoking status. [If the applicable policy version contains additional non-indication criteria not quoted above, I ask that Cigna identify them specifically so they can be addressed.]

Conclusion

Taken together, the record — 24 months of progressive symptoms, MRI-confirmed Kellgren-Lawrence Grade IV medial compartment disease with bone-on-bone changes, functional impairment affecting stair climbing and sleep, and failure of more than three months of multimodal conservative management — supports medical necessity for CPT 27446 as described in the criteria I was able to obtain from Cigna's own delegated review guideline, CMM-311. I ask that Cigna:

1. Reverse the denial and authorize CPT 27446; or, in the alternative,
2. Identify in writing the specific policy version and criterion element that Cigna contends is not met, so that Dr. Lindqvist and I may submit the precise supplemental documentation needed (including quantified range-of-motion/stability findings and walking-distance limitation, as noted above).

I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in the denial notice (due by 2027-01-28). I understand Cigna's Arizona Health Care Insurer Appeals Process Information Packet separately states that some Arizona-regulated plans allow up to two years to begin the appeals process; out of caution, I am filing well within the shorter 180-day period stated in my denial letter.

Please treat this as a standard internal appeal. [If applicable, please advise whether this matter qualifies for expedited review under Arizona's expedited appeal process for prior authorization denials.] I authorize Dr. Lindqvist's office to submit supplemental clinical documentation directly in support of this appeal, and I have asked his office to send an addendum addressing the range-of-motion, stability, and ambulation-distance details noted above.

Enclosed/attached with this appeal:
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-01 (Ref. POC-8AD74FF769-66861)
- MRI report dated 2026-06-08
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-12 to 2026-07-07, 24 visits)
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-05-18)
- Office/exam notes documenting provocative testing and range-of-motion findings
- [Supplemental surgeon addendum, once received]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing and provide the name and contact information of the reviewer assigned to this case. If you have any questions or require additional information, please contact me at [phone number] or [email address], or my authorized representative, Dr. Lindqvist's office, at [office phone number].

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Reese Mercado
